workflows.name: Follow a run's live event stream
workflows.ui_action: Automatic after send / on opening a conversation
workflows.authorization: token when an operator token is configured (X-Mucaro-Token / Bearer), otherwise loopback-only with Host/Origin guard; remote peers always need a token (backend/app/main.py:323-333, backend/app/auth.py:29, backend/app/auth.py:74, backend/app/auth.py:135)
workflows.status_evidence: Stream parsed in api.js:171-226 and merged by seq (ChatView.jsx:141-147); text_delta events concatenated into the answer (feed.js:83-85). Defect by source reading (not run): on a 'final'/'approval_request'/'question'/'error' event the client replaces the run's event list with GET /work-runs/{id}/events (ChatView.jsx:148-150, 127-131), which is called with no limit (api.js:280) and the endpoint defaults to limit=500 (main.py:1051). A live-streamed answer emits one text_delta event per provider delta (work_runs.py:1217-1219, model_router.py:1000), so a run with more than 500 events is cut to its first 500 after completion and on every reload (ChatView.jsx:196-206 catches up once, then the same replacement happens). No test exercises a run with more than 500 events.

workflows.name: Stop the current turn

workflows.authorization: token when an operator token is configured (X-Mucaro-Token / Bearer), otherwise loopback-only with Host/Origin guard; remote peers always need a token (backend/app/main.py:323-333, backend/app/auth.py:29, backend/app/auth.py:74, backend/app/auth.py:135)
workflows.status_evidence: UI -> api.stopRun (api.js:282) -> stop_run (work_runs.py:581). Waiting runs are finalized at once (work_runs.py:609-613). A RUNNING run only records cancel_requested (work_runs.py:603); it is honoured between phases and inside the tools phase (work_runs.py:773, 921). The answer phase has no checkpoint and _complete sets COMPLETED unconditionally (work_runs.py:1204-1290, 1363-1371), so Stop pressed while the answer is streaming does not abort generation. The client does not abort its own stream either (ChatView.jsx:314-323).

accessibility_source_findings.finding: At <=760px (which the 420px-wide desktop window reaches) the closed navigation panel is only translated off-screen; it is not display:none, visibility:hidden or inert. Its ~10+ buttons stay in the tab order and the accessibility tree, so keyboard focus disappears off-screen before reaching the page content. When open it is not a dialog: no focus move into it, no focus trap, no Escape, no close button, and the toggle keeps the label 'Open navigation'.

Functional, affects all users: runs with more than 500 events are reloaded with only the first 500 (see workflow stream-answer), which removes the tail of a long live-streamed answer and its citations.

The conversation menu declares role=menu/menuitem but implements none of the pattern: focus is not moved into it, there is no arrow-key navigation, Escape or outside-click close; it stays open until an item or the toggle is pressed.

The mode picker is a ul role=listbox whose children are plain li elements wrapping button role=option (invalid ownership), with no arrow keys, Escape or active-descendant; it works as a list of buttons by Tab only.

Sheet returns focus to the element focused when it mounted. For sheets opened from the conversation menu (Rename, Delete, Background tasks) that element is a menu item that has already been unmounted, so focus falls to the document body on close. Same for the approval card: after Allow/Deny the card unmounts and nothing receives focus.

The trap's focusable selector omits <summary> and matches elements inside closed <details> (e.g. pre[tabindex=0]). In sheets that end with disclosures (Tool activity, Evidence) the computed last item can be an unfocusable hidden element, so Tab from the last visible control can leave the dialog; the page behind is not inert or aria-hidden (aria-modal only).
Switching workspace does not move focus, change document.title or announce; a screen-reader user gets only aria-current on the pressed button. The page title is always 'Mucaro AI'.

A pending approval is announced through the polite live region ('Waiting for your approval.') but focus is not moved to the card and it is not a live region itself; the user must find it in the feed. Deny and Allow once are native buttons, so keyboard activation works.
Provenance, Sources, Memory and Background tasks show their empty text while the first load is still in flight (no loading state).

DirectoryIntake errors render in a div with no role=alert, its buttons have no type attribute, and the status badge is raw status code text; the section is titled 'Add a folder from this Mac' on every platform.
Rebuild index and the memory On/Off toggle have no error handling; a failure is invisible and inaudible.
When Adjust/Revise fails, the error text is rendered on the card behind the modal sheet, not inside it.

Present in source: skip link, lang=en, global :focus-visible outline, prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-color-scheme, 16px fields and 44px targets at <=900px or coarse pointers, labelled form fields, role=alert on errors, one polite live region.

special_adjudications.question: 1. Six workspaces: exact list and mounted component for each
special_adjudications.answer: Confirmed, exactly six, in this order in the WORKSPACES registry: Chat -> ChatView; Workbench -> WorkbenchWorkspace; Sources -> SourcesWorkspace; Memory -> MemoryWorkspace; Provenance -> ProvenanceWorkspace; Settings -> SettingsWorkspace. Each is rendered only when health.state is 'ok' and view equals its id. 'Background tasks' is a seventh item in the same nav list but opens a drawer, not a workspace. While the service wants a token, TokenGate replaces all six.

special_adjudications.question: 2. Provenance workspace: fully functional, partial or presentational; ledger reconciliation
special_adjudications.answer: Functional but read-only and narrow; not presentational. It has no props, no buttons, inputs, links or handlers of its own: the only controls are one native <details>/<summary> 'Record' per tool call. On mount it makes two calls. GET /tools/summary returns counts by status computed from the stored tool-call records plus a live verification of the hash-chained audit log; the UI shows 'Verified (N events)' or the broken status and reason in error styling. GET /tools/requests returns every stored tool call; the UI lists them newest first with status, tool name, created time and, behind the disclosure, requested_by, approved_by, denied_by, argument digest, run id and raw arguments/result JSON. Both are real persisted data. Limits: loaded once (no refresh, filter, pagination, loading state or link to the run); the audit events themselves (GET /tools/audit) are never shown; 'who decided' is the constant 'api' for every GUI decision and 'policy:auto-local-read-only' for auto approvals; it shows nothing about source provenance, message-edit originals (which the chat UI says are 'preserved in provenance') or execution-entry receipts. Acceptance ledger is _architecture/release/acceptance_ledger_v1.json. TGT-032 'Provenance inspection' (IMPLEMENTED / PASS, note 'Verified audit chain, per-action records behind disclosure') matches the component exactly; its positive gate is a rendered check that waits for 'Verified (N events)' and then records a literal true. TGT-014 'Governed tool execution' lists the component and is supported by a rendered check that the Record shows requested_by 'model'. TGT-003 'Specialized workspaces' (PARTIAL / OPEN) says 'Sources/Memory/Settings exist; GIS/OCR/Code/Provenance/Artifacts surfaces absent': stale and contradicted by current source and by TGT-032, since Provenance and Workbench are both mounted. INV-018 'Provenance' (PARTIAL / PROVISIONAL) is about backend provenance records on ingested sources, not this workspace; those records are shown in the Evidence sheet and Sources detail, not here. MATRIX-015 lists provenance among 70 rendered checks; no axe run covers the Provenance view. No acceptance or ledger entries about Provenance were found in .mucaro/ or qa/ other than the rendered script.

special_adjudications.question: 3. Mobile: breakpoints and narrow-viewport behaviour (window min 420x560); workspace switcher and background-tasks drawer
special_adjudications.answer: Three media rules. (a) max-width 760px: single-column shell, off-canvas sidebar, top bar with hamburger, tighter paddings, execution-entry buttons stretch to 44px, user bubble 92% wide, and every Sheet becomes a bottom sheet (full width, max-height 88vh, rounded top). (b) max-width 900px or pointer:coarse: 16px form fields and 44px minimum control height. (c) prefers-reduced-motion. Safe-area insets are applied to sidebar, top bar, composer and sheet body. The native window minimum (420x560) is below 760px, so the desktop app shows the phone layout when narrowed. The workspace switcher has no separate mobile form: it is the same six buttons inside the off-canvas sidebar, reached through the hamburger; picking one closes the panel. Background tasks is a button in that panel (and in the conversation menu); on a narrow screen it opens as a bottom sheet over the page, with focus trap, Escape and backdrop close from Sheet. No workspace has its own breakpoint rules; they rely on flex wrapping. Gaps: the closed panel stays focusable (see accessibility findings), no Escape or close button for the panel, composer Enter inserts a newline on coarse pointers by design. Rendered evidence exists for 390x844 and 393/430/720 widths only; nothing renders at 420x560, and the ledger marks software-keyboard avoidance OPEN (MOB-F01).

special_adjudications.question: 4. Keyboard: shortcuts, composer behaviour, focus order, reachability
special_adjudications.answer: Shortcuts are local only (listed in keyboard_shortcuts); there are no global accelerators and none for switching workspace. Composer: Enter sends, Shift+Enter is a newline, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter always sends; on a coarse pointer Enter is a newline and only the button or Cmd/Ctrl+Enter sends. IME safe: the handler returns early when event.nativeEvent.isComposing is true or keyCode is 229. Empty text cannot be sent; focus returns to the textarea after sending. Focus order follows the DOM: skip link, sidebar (New chat, six workspaces, Background tasks, filter, conversations), then main (hamburger on narrow screens, service banner Retry, workspace content); in Chat: Model, Repository, conversation menu, feed controls, queued items, textarea, Mode, Stop, Send. All six workspaces and the tasks drawer are native buttons, so every workspace is reachable by keyboard alone at desktop width. At <=760px they are still reachable, but through an off-screen panel whose focus is invisible unless the hamburger is pressed first. View changes do not move focus.

special_adjudications.question: 5. Modals/drawers: role, aria-modal, labelling, focus trap, Escape, focus return
special_adjudications.answer: Eleven overlays, all built on one Sheet component: Background tasks, Tool activity, Evidence [n] (right drawers / bottom sheets); Rename conversation, Delete conversation?, Remove this source?, Delete this memory?, Revoke folder access?, Save answer, Execution receipt, Adjust goal / Revise plan (centred). Sheet gives each role=dialog, aria-modal=true, aria-labelledby pointing at its h2 title, a labelled close button, initial focus on a data-autofocus field or the dialog itself, a Tab/Shift+Tab trap, Escape to close, backdrop mousedown to close, and focus return to the element focused at mount. Confirm sheets focus the cancel button and ignore close while busy. Weaknesses: the background is not inert; the trap selector omits summary and can pick hidden elements; focus return fails when the opener was a menu item that has unmounted. Three overlays are not dialogs: the mobile navigation panel, the conversation menu (role=menu) and the mode picker (role=listbox); none has Escape, a trap or focus return. The inline 'Confirm Directory Access' block is not a dialog.

special_adjudications.question: 6. Streaming: rendering, cancel, mid-stream error or disconnect, partial output
special_adjudications.answer: Rendering: the client reads server-sent events with fetch, de-duplicates by seq and concatenates text_delta events into the answer, rendered as inert text with fenced code blocks; the run article is aria-busy while RUNNING and the feed auto-scrolls only when already near the bottom. The streaming text is not a live region; 'Answer complete.' is announced at the end. Save and Share appear only on terminal runs; Copy and Edit are offered while still streaming. Cancel: Stop calls POST /work-runs/{id}/stop. Waiting runs stop at once; a running run is flagged and stops at the next phase boundary, but the answer phase has no checkpoint, so Stop does not interrupt text that is already streaming and the run still ends COMPLETED. Model/provider error mid-answer: the backend records error and final(FAILED) events; text_delta events already written stay in the log, so the partial text remains above an alert showing category, status and detail, and 'The turn failed.' is announced. Disconnect: a stream that fails, closes without an end event or is silent for 25 s is retried with backoff (reloading the run from the event log each time); after 10 failures a 'Live updates paused' notice with Resume appears; the app-level banner shows 'Reconnecting…' from the 15 s health poll, and returning to the page or regaining network forces a re-follow. Partial output is preserved because events are persisted server-side. A service restart marks running runs INTERRUPTED. Defect by source reading: runs with more than 500 events are reloaded truncated to the first 500 (see workflow stream-answer).

special_adjudications.question: 7. Approval workflows: Planning-to-Execution Gate and tool-request approval
special_adjudications.answer: Tool-request approval is complete. The card is a labelled region ('Permission request for <tool>') showing the tool, who asked, arguments (patches as a diff) and the argument digest, with native Deny and Allow once buttons. They POST /tools/requests/{id}/approve or /deny with arguments_sha256. The backend refuses a non-pending call or a digest mismatch, stores status with approved_by/denied_by and a timestamp on the tool-call record, appends a hash-chained audit event, and resumes the run. Both buttons work from the keyboard; the waiting state is announced ('Waiting for your approval.') and the decision is announced ('Allowed/Denied <tool>.') through the polite live region, and the conversation list shows 'Needs your approval'. Focus is not moved to the card and is lost when it disappears. The actor recorded is the constant 'api'. The Planning-to-Execution Gate named in README and docs/EXECUTION_GATE.md (POST /plan, POST /approve) has no GUI: the Workbench only compiles a plan with approval NOT_REQUESTED and states that nothing is executed. The GUI gate that does exist is the execution-entry card: Proceed/Execute and Adjust/Revise post a decision bound to artifact, revision, expected version, source commit and an idempotency key; the decision and receipt hashes are persisted and shown in the Execution receipt sheet. The primary button is natively disabled with an aria-describedby reason until the entry is ready and the source identity is current, it activates from the keyboard, and 'Execution started.' is announced. But the GUI can neither create an entry nor mark one ready, so this gate is usable only for entries prepared through the API.

denominator.coverage_statement: Exhaustive: every file under frontend/src was read in full (App, api, feed, files, clipboard, all 22 components) except Icons.jsx, nextVectorOptions.js and the lower part of threadActivity.js, which hold no surfaces; workspaces, navigation items, dialogs/drawers, settings, context actions, keyboard handlers and all 77 backend routes in backend/app/main.py are enumerated exhaustively. Forms, lists and panels inside each workspace are enumerated to the level of each distinct control group (believed exhaustive for controls, not for every read-only field). Backend handlers were read for auth, execution entry, workbench plan, conversations, messages, work-run events/stream/stop, memory, tools and exports; deeper modules (cli.py, model_router.py, execution_entry.py, GIS/OCR/coding) were sampled by grep only. Test references were found by grep and not executed; has_test=false means no test was found by the searches run, not proof of absence. Nothing was run, so every status is from source reading.
